conbody.p: A troubleshooting section is recognized by a problem-oriented heading such as "The Printer Does Not Power On" or "Print Jobs Fail to Complete," paired with a body that presents a condition, a cause, and a corrective action. The converter looks for bold labels in the form Cause: and Remedy: in the body. Both the heading and the body labels must be present. A problem-oriented heading without cause and remedy labels causes the converter to classify the section as Task or Generic depending on the body structure.

When these signals align, the converter generates a <troubleshooting> element with <troublebody>. The problem heading maps to <title> and the condition text maps to <condition>. Each cause label and its associated text maps to <cause> inside a <troubleSolution> block. Each remedy label and its associated steps maps to <remedy> inside the same <troubleSolution> block, with each <li> mapping to <step><cmd>. When a section contains multiple cause-and-remedy pairs, the converter generates one <condition> at the top of <troublebody> and a separate <troubleSolution> for each pair. The condition is not repeated for each solution.
